items.text: – See what a fine mess you've made, you shit-for-brains.
items.q: Eskandar turns on Amir angrily. Does this sound natural?
before: Eskandar turned toward me and leaned his head and chest forward in my direction. His eyes were wide, and he said in a rough voice that had lost none of its Alain Delon quality:

items.text: – What kind of shit is going on in that brain of yours now?
items.q: Hooman reacts to Amir's odd question about dreams. Does this sound natural?
before: – Hooman, has this ever happened to you? In a dream, you tell someone about something, and afterward you start wondering whether the first thing was a nightmare or a memory?

items.text: From what I gathered from the post, he'd become a physics teacher at one of the high schools in his town, and that deluded dipshit had been teaching his own theories instead of the material in the book.
items.q: Hooman laughs about a former roommate. Does 'deluded dipshit' sound natural?

items.text: As soon as your name comes up, my ears prick up.
items.q: Amir admits to Niloofar that he listens out for her name. Does this sound natural?
before: – Well, when I'm sitting around the department, I listen for your name in the other students' conversations.

items.text: – Ugh, what do you want, Eskandar? What the hell is wrong with you?
items.q: Hooman snaps at Eskandar, who has just mocked his name. Does this sound natural?
before: – Do you really think that name suits you? This hairy body, this face armed to the teeth with beard and hair. If you're Hooman, then I'm Susan.

items.text: – No name suits you, damn you.
items.q: Hooman shouts back at Eskandar. Does this sound natural?
before: His voice grew louder, and he said:

items.text: – I'm telling you I can't see, asshole.
items.q: Sajad, who can't see without his glasses, snaps at Farid. Does it sound like friendly dorm swearing?
before: – The end. Watch the end. See how fast it runs away. It tore up the spider's house too. I didn't name it The Documentary of the Cockroach That Wrecked the Spider's House for nothing.

items.text: – I'm looking for my glasses, asshole. Tell Farid to stop leaving his cup right in my way.
items.q: Short-sighted Sajad stumbles around the room again. Does his grumble sound natural?

items.text: – I would have preferred rooming with them instead of a dick-brain like you.

items.text: – Again we reach that same damned discontinuity.

items.text: – Pfff, donkey, who knows better, the friend of the cousin of our brother-in-law's master craftsman who is the richest man in Tehran, or you, you calf?
items.q: Hamid, a boy, angrily calls his friend 'donkey' and 'calf'. Does it sound like a boy's angry insult?
Sajad picks up on the running joke about the cousin. Is his short question clear?

That was when Taghi felt like messing with me again.

items.text: – If there'd been black, I'd have picked black. The friend of the cousin of our brother-in-law's master craftsman who is the richest man in Tehran says black is the color of love.
